questions.question: Which finding in a patient with AD requires urgent reassessment rather than a routine topical refill?
choices: Painful grouped facial erosions with fever and malaise
Stable dry flexural patches
A request for moisturizer options
Improved sleep after a flare
questions.explanation: Painful vesicular/erosive rash with systemic symptoms can indicate eczema herpeticum or another serious infection and requires urgent evaluation.

questions.question: What is a core component of AD treatment?
choices: Regular bland moisturization and barrier repair
Routine systemic corticosteroids for long-term control
Elimination diets for every patient
Topical antibiotics for every flare
questions.explanation: Moisturization supports barrier function and is foundational AD therapy; other measures are individualized.

questions.question: Why should a clinician ask about sleep in AD?
choices: Itch and skin disease can substantially impair sleep, function, mood, and quality of life
Sleep is unrelated to eczema
Only children have sleep effects
Sleep history replaces skin examination
questions.explanation: Sleep loss is a major clinical outcome of AD and can guide treatment intensity and support needs.

questions.question: What is an important principle for topical corticosteroid use in AD?
choices: Match potency, vehicle, site, amount, and duration to the patient and teach technique
Use the strongest product everywhere indefinitely
Avoid all anti-inflammatory treatment because of fear
Apply a household member’s prescription
questions.explanation: Topical steroid selection and education should be individualized, especially for thin/sensitive skin sites.

questions.question: When can patch testing be useful?
choices: Persistent or distribution-specific dermatitis when allergic contact dermatitis is suspected
Every new dry patch regardless of history
To diagnose bacterial infection
Instead of assessing exposures
questions.explanation: Patch testing can help identify allergic contact dermatitis in selected persistent or refractory patterns.

questions.question: Which statement about topical antimicrobials in AD is most accurate?
choices: They are not a routine substitute for barrier and anti-inflammatory treatment when no infection is present
They cure all eczema
They should be used on every dry patch
They replace infection assessment
questions.explanation: Guidance does not support routine topical antimicrobial use for uninfected AD; treat infection based on clinical assessment.

questions.question: Which symptom suggests that a rash may not be routine eczema?
choices: Severe pain out of proportion with systemic symptoms or rapidly spreading warmth
Stable itch relieved by moisturizer
A familiar chronic pattern without change
Improved skin hydration
questions.explanation: Pain, systemic illness, rapid spread, or warmth can indicate infection or another serious process needing reassessment.

questions.question: When is dermatology referral reasonable for AD?
choices: Uncertain diagnosis, extensive/refractory disease, recurrent infection, major sleep/function impact, or need for advanced therapy
Only when the rash has completely resolved
For every moisturizer refill
Never for eyelid disease
questions.explanation: Complex, refractory, high-burden, or diagnostically unclear AD benefits from dermatology collaboration.

questions.question: What should be checked when a patient reports that AD treatment failed?
choices: What was used, where/how often, affordability, adverse effects, technique, exposures, and diagnosis
Only the prescription date
Only the patient’s age
Nothing if the rash is chronic
questions.explanation: Apparent treatment failure often reflects technique, access, irritant/contact exposure, infection, or an alternative diagnosis.

questions.question: What is the FNP-level AD principle?
choices: Treat every rash as the same disorder
Integrate rash morphology, emergency safety, barrier care, anti-inflammatory technique, function, and access
Use one topical medication for every body site
Ignore eye and mucosal symptoms
questions.explanation: High-quality AD care combines correct diagnosis, red-flag triage, individualized treatment, and practical longitudinal support.
